items.evidence: Recorded deviation: 1,000-hand test is opt-in (TLH_SLOW_TESTS) with a 100-hand every-push version using the same assertions; judged on substance. TLH_SLOW_TESTS=1 run: the 1,000-hand TAG test passes; it asserts violations 0, full action-list deep-equality, equal final.result, user hands >= 100 and bot actions >= 1,000. Holdout (own seeds: table 4242, user 31337): 1,000 TAG hands, seat 1 on shared random moves; all 1,000 replays match action-by-action (seat, type, amount; 8,741 bot actions compared), 0 violations, equal results; 970 hands with a user decision.

Same recorded deviation as SPEC-01. Opt-in 1,000-hand Mixed test passes and asserts every style acted. Holdout: 1,000 Mixed hands (seed 4242) match fully (10,904 bot actions; TAG 3,291, Calling station 3,643, Maniac 2,691, Rock 1,279), including 9 hands with replaced bots (30 actions by replaced seats); a second 1,000-hand Mixed run (seed 99, 4 replacement hands), 500 Tough hands and 400 Mixed sng hands (empty seats via recordStacks) also match with 0 violations. Re-deciding check: replaying with the bot styles swapped to Maniac changes the actions in 190/200 hands, and mutants A and D are caught.

Acceptance test passes over 200 Mixed hands with a user decision and asserts hole cards, board prefix, the pre-user action prefix, alt equality and type difference. Holdout: 400 Mixed hands with my own change (a random different legal first action, then random user moves): every hand keeps the same hole cards, board prefix and identical bot actions before seat 1's first action, 0 violations; all 400 replays diverge afterwards, so the check is not trivial.

Recorded deviation: userPolicy is a HandSetup/PlaytestOptions field instead of a PlaytestSeams key (the locked TASK-6.9 test pins the seam keys); judged on substance. Unit test passes: the factory is called once with (code, 1), makePolicy only for seats 2-6, seat-1 views reach the user policy, and runPlaytest Mixed calls it once per hand with seat 1. Holdout: 300-hand Mixed run with userPolicy = seededTagPolicy has records deep-equal to a run without it (bot seats keep their line-up styles). Mutants B and C are killed.

Unit test passes and asserts order, the exact RangeError message, then-delegation and the empty-script delegation. Holdout: a script one action short makes replayWithBots throw RangeError('No recorded action left for seat 1'); the same script replayed twice is deterministic.

Unit test passes: an sng record without seat 3 gives recordStacks index 2 = 0, the replay record equals the original, and a check facing the blind gives a legal-action violation. Holdout: recordStacks for [0,1500,900,0,2100,1500] round-trips; with seat 1 not dealt in, the user policy is never called and the replay matches; an illegal raise amount is reported as a legal-action violation; the replay's number is 1. cli.test.ts passes in the full suite.

The default 10,000-hand seed-42 run's SHA-256 is 442dbf55bd32d87a5e367d3c5b9be28ec9303c57174783eae5947134aa408fbc (matches main). The Mixed run shows 'Invariant violations: 0', exits 0, and its full output is byte-identical to the base commit.

npm run lint (eslint + prettier) exit 0; npm run typecheck exit 0; npm test exit 0 with coverage thresholds holding (gate run 97.36% statements); boundary tests are in the passing suite; CI run 45063252542 succeeded.

grep for fetch(/XMLHttpRequest/WebSocket in src/playtest finds nothing (exit 1); backlog doc list --plain shows doc-85 'TASK-6.15: Replay any hand with every bot acting exactly as before'. No UI or strategy changes in the diff.

findings.expected_vs_actual: Expected the AC#1/AC#2 replay tests to show on their own that bots re-decide. Actual: a replay that re-applied the recorded bot actions, or a playHand that ignored userPolicy everywhere, would still pass the AC#1/AC#2 tests. Only the AC#3 and unit tests catch these. The suite as a whole catches every mutant I tried, so this does not block.
findings.fix: Optional: add an assertion to the SPEC-01/02 tests that a replay with a changed bot line-up or changed user actions diverges, so each test proves re-decision on its own.

summary: All 9 SPEC items PASS. Full suite green (635 passed), the opt-in 1,000-hand runs pass, and my own 1,000-hand TAG and Mixed replays (different seeds, replaced bots included, plus Tough and sng) match every bot action in order and amount. AC#3 holds with my own changed first actions. Mutation checks confirm that replayWithBots re-decides and that the seam touches only seat 1. The default playtest SHA and the Mixed output are unchanged, test integrity is clean and CI is green. Both recorded deviations (field instead of seam; 1,000-hand runs opt-in) keep the substance of the spec. One LOW non-blocking finding.
